quotes.text: Three lean boats, send less. One fat boat after lean ones, send full again
*Never send nothing, for nothing is a door nailed shut.
Give to the closed hand what it gave you.
*Match what is poured, measure for measure.
But watch for the first jar — and when it comes, empty the cistern.*
Forgive twice, never thrice.
So I paid them exactly what they poured: nothing.
Forgiveness is for the mist. Memory is for the hand. One lean boat is weather. Three lean boats is weather no longer.
They carved the fifth law last
Thereafter every measure was spoken aloud before it was poured, and every return was spoken after
I made the mist so you would learn to judge the heart, not the grain.
because someone must open the river, and the one who refuses to open it has closed it for everyone.
"Then you teach hoarding."

note: Mirror Stone laws: forgive mist, never nothing (R6), then hardens to measure for measure and silence for takers, reopening at first jar.

quotes.text: If mist distorts one crossing, wait for a pattern; if greed repeats, withdraw without spite.
After the third, shorten the rope—but leave one lamp lit, so repentance still has a harbor.
“Forgive the first loss,” Aster answered, “for fog confuses honest hands. Remember the second.
She marked the broken crossing upon a stone and kept her next kernels nearer home.
Test the unknown with one coal. Trust the proven with the harvest. Forgive mist once, punish patterns slowly
Yet Mira, haunted by older losses, sent him an empty ferry.
Later Orun approached with a record of brave gifts and fair divisions, but she kept all five amber kernels.
In the first, every traveler punished the next for an earlier wound; soon no ferries moved
“Mist bends measures. Never condemn one uncertain crossing; watch the pattern.
The river darkened, for words without deeds were hollow reeds.
Mira asked, “Must I always surrender everything?”
But never make innocence repay a stranger’s debt.

note: Mira repeatedly sends empty ferries to fair-record keepers from old losses; Aster corrects; repeated greed shortens the rope, lamp left lit.
